notes: Community pack, roadmap Phase 1 candidate. 5 tracks x 10 themes x 5 grade bands = 250 blocks. Expanded by tools/generate_pack.py.

tracks.name: Law: the system you already live in

themes.description: Constitutions, statutes, regulations, case law and bylaws — the layers of law and which one governs the thing in front of you.
themes.transfer_check: For one everyday rule that binds you, identify which layer of law it comes from and find its actual text.

themes.description: Who sues whom, who prosecutes, and why the same act can be both — the two systems' different players, standards and stakes.
themes.transfer_check: Sort five real scenarios into civil, criminal or both, naming the parties and the standard of proof for each.

themes.description: What courtrooms actually do all day — the hierarchy, who the people in it are, and what an ordinary hearing looks like.
themes.transfer_check: Observe a real public hearing (in person or official stream) and report who did what, in the correct terms.

themes.description: Legal research for civilians: official sources, current versions, and the difference between the law and a blog about the law.
themes.transfer_check: Answer one real legal question about your own life from primary official sources, citing the provision itself.

themes.description: Limitation periods, notice windows and appeal clocks — why being right runs out, and diarising the dates that matter.
themes.transfer_check: For three real claim types, find the applicable time limit where you live and compute the deadline from a given event date.

themes.description: Legal aid, law centres, pro bono, ombudsmen and fixed-fee clinics — the map of low-cost help and who qualifies.
themes.transfer_check: Map the free and low-cost legal help available for one problem type at your own address, with eligibility rules verified.

themes.description: Setting out a grievance formally: facts, ask, deadline — the letter that resolves most disputes before any court sees them.
themes.transfer_check: Draft a complete letter before action for a real or realistic dispute, meeting the format a court would later respect.

themes.theme: Small claims: court without the lawyers
themes.description: The small-claims track end to end — filing, fees, evidence bundles and the hearing where you speak for yourself.
themes.transfer_check: Prepare a complete mock small claim: forms filled, evidence bundled, and your three-minute case stated aloud.

themes.theme: Mediation and the deal that beats the verdict
themes.description: Negotiated and mediated settlement — why most disputes should end in a room, not a courtroom, and how to settle well.
themes.transfer_check: Take one side of a role-played dispute through a structured mediation to a written settlement both sides sign.

themes.theme: When the law itself is the problem
themes.description: Challenging rules: consultation responses, judicial review in outline, and the civic route from unjust rule to changed rule.
themes.transfer_check: Find one live consultation or proposed rule affecting you and submit (or fully draft) a reasoned formal response.

themes.description: Offer, acceptance, consideration, intention — the ingredients that turn words into obligations, including the ones spoken aloud.
themes.transfer_check: Analyse five everyday exchanges and rule which formed a contract, naming the missing ingredient where none did.

themes.description: A method for real documents: parties, obligations, money, term, exit, liability — the six answers to extract from any contract.
themes.transfer_check: Extract the six-answer summary from a real contract you are actually subject to, in one page a friend could rely on.

themes.description: Auto-renewal, unilateral change, arbitration, indemnity, liquidated damages — the standard traps and the flags they fly.
themes.transfer_check: Locate and explain three bite-clauses across real contracts or terms of service, and state what each costs you if triggered.

themes.theme: Terms of service: the contract nobody reads
themes.description: What you actually agree to online — licences to your content, data terms, termination at will — and the summaries that surface it.
themes.transfer_check: Audit the terms of one service you use daily and report the three most consequential things you had agreed to unknowingly.

themes.description: What is negotiable (more than you think), asking in writing, and the walk-away number decided in advance.
themes.transfer_check: Negotiate one real agreement's term (price, date, clause) with the exchange documented, or run the full role-play to signed changes.

themes.theme: Breach: when the other side fails
themes.description: Material versus minor breach, mitigation, and the remedies ladder from cure period to damages.
themes.transfer_check: For a real or case-study breach, classify it, state your mitigation duty, and draft the remedy demand in the right order.

themes.description: Cancellation rights, cooling-off periods, termination clauses and the exit executed cleanly versus the exit that costs you.
themes.transfer_check: Exit or mock-exit one real subscription or agreement using its own terms, on time, in writing, with proof retained.

themes.theme: Deposits, guarantees and standing behind others
themes.description: Security deposits, guarantors and co-signing — the promises that activate when someone else fails.
themes.transfer_check: Explain a real guarantee or deposit's exact trigger and exposure, and advise a role-played friend asked to co-sign, with reasons.

themes.theme: The informal deal with family and friends
themes.description: Loans to brothers, flats shared with friends — why the closest deals need the clearest writing, and the note that saves the relationship.
themes.transfer_check: Draft a fair one-page written agreement for a real or realistic informal arrangement between people who trust each other.

themes.theme: Signing for the future: powers and wills
themes.description: Powers of attorney, advance decisions and wills — the documents that speak when you cannot, and what happens without them.
themes.transfer_check: Complete the will-and-powers checklist for a named adult: what exists, what is missing, and the exact route to fix one gap.

tracks.name: The consumer: buying, returning, being made whole

themes.theme: What you are owed when you buy
themes.description: Satisfactory quality, as described, fit for purpose — the rights attached to every purchase whether the shop likes it or not.
themes.transfer_check: For three real purchases, state the statutory rights attached to each and the remedy ladder if it fails.

themes.description: The store's goodwill policy and your legal rights are different things — knowing which you are invoking and when each is stronger.
themes.transfer_check: Handle one real or staged return correctly, explicitly identifying whether you used policy or law, and why.

themes.description: Repair, replace, refund — the sequence, the burden of proof windows, and the evidence to gather before the second failure.
themes.transfer_check: Run a real or mock faulty-goods claim through the full sequence in writing, with the evidence file that wins it.

themes.description: Reasonable care and skill — holding builders, salons, garages and installers to the standard, and pricing the put-right.
themes.transfer_check: Draft the complaint and remedy demand for a real or case-study substandard service, quantifying the cost to cure.

themes.description: Online, phone and doorstep purchases — the cooling-off rights, the return-shipping rules and the exceptions that surprise.
themes.transfer_check: Exercise (or fully mock) a cooling-off cancellation for an online purchase inside its window, with the notices done right.

themes.description: Card protections, chargeback windows and why how you pay changes what you can recover when it goes wrong.
themes.transfer_check: File or fully draft one chargeback or card-protection claim with the transaction evidence assembled to standard.

themes.description: Escalation done properly: the right person, the factual timeline, the specific ask and the deadline — firm without fury.
themes.transfer_check: Write and send (or finalise) a real complaint with timeline, evidence, ask and deadline, and log the response against it.

themes.theme: The ombudsman and the free referee
themes.description: Sector ombudsmen and ADR schemes — the free escalation most consumers never use, and how to hand them a winnable file.
themes.transfer_check: Identify the correct ombudsman for one real dispute type and prepare the complete referral file to its requirements.

themes.description: Fake shops, counterfeit goods, subscription traps and recovery scams — the purchase that was never a purchase.
themes.transfer_check: Autopsy one real scam listing or trap: mark its tells, state the reporting channels used, and the victim's actual recovery options.

themes.theme: Debt collection and your actual obligations
themes.description: What collectors may and may not do, statute-barred debt, and the difference between owing and being harassed.
themes.transfer_check: Respond to a real or scripted collection letter correctly: verify the debt, know the rules the collector must follow, and draft the reply.

tracks.name: Work: the deal behind the job

themes.description: The status categories, the rights attached to each, and the misclassification that quietly removes protections.
themes.transfer_check: Classify three real working arrangements (yours or case studies) by status and list two rights that change across them.

themes.description: Pay, hours, notice, probation, restrictive covenants — reading the job offer as the contract it is.
themes.transfer_check: Produce the six-answer summary of a real employment contract or offer, flagging any clause you would question before signing.

themes.description: Minimum wage arithmetic, payslip reading, unlawful deductions and the overtime that never appears.
themes.transfer_check: Audit a real payslip against contract and law — rate, hours, deductions — and draft the query for any discrepancy found.

themes.description: Working time limits, rest rights and the pressure to be always available — the boundaries the law already drew.
themes.transfer_check: Compare one real working pattern to the applicable limits and rest rights, and script the conversation any breach requires.

themes.theme: Leave: the time that is yours
themes.description: Holiday, sickness, parental and carer leave — what accrues, what needs notice and what cannot be refused.
themes.transfer_check: Compute a real worker's leave entitlement for the year and correctly process (or mock) one request and one sickness absence.

themes.description: The protected characteristics, direct and indirect discrimination, and reasonable adjustment as a right rather than a favour.
themes.transfer_check: Analyse two case-study workplace scenarios: identify the protected ground, the discrimination type, and the remedy route for each.

themes.description: Naming it, logging it, reporting it — the evidence diary and the routes inside and beyond the employer.
themes.transfer_check: Build a correct incident log from a scripted harassment scenario and map its escalation route through and past the employer.

themes.description: Investigations, hearings, accompaniment and appeals — what a fair procedure owes you when the employer moves against you.
themes.transfer_check: Role-play the employee side of a disciplinary hearing with a companion, exercising each procedural right at the correct moment.

themes.description: Notice, redundancy rules, unfair dismissal and the settlement agreement — the endings, and the rights attached to each.
themes.transfer_check: For one real or case-study dismissal, determine its type, the entitlements owed, and the challenge deadline, with the first letter drafted.

themes.description: Unions, collective bargaining and protected activity — what workers may lawfully do together and how that changes the deal.
themes.transfer_check: Find the recognised union or body for one real workplace and explain what protected steps starting to organise there would involve.

themes.description: The charter, constitution or convention where you live — the actual named rights, and what each does and does not protect.
themes.transfer_check: For your own jurisdiction, list the instrument and five named rights, matching each to one real situation it governs.

themes.description: Stop, search and questioning — what officers may require, what you must provide, and the calm scripts that protect everyone.
themes.transfer_check: Role-play two police encounters correctly: state your actual obligations, exercise your actual rights, and note the record to make after.

themes.theme: Arrest and the hours that follow
themes.description: The caution, the phone call, the duty lawyer and the custody clock — the rights that exist precisely when you are least able to look them up.
themes.transfer_check: Recite and apply the post-arrest rights sequence for your jurisdiction in a staged scenario, including invoking the duty lawyer.

themes.description: Assembly and speech rights, notification rules, police powers at protests and the line where protection ends.
themes.transfer_check: Plan a lawful demonstration for a cause: the notifications, the rules on route and sound, and the legal-observer arrangements.

themes.theme: Your file: what the state holds
themes.description: Records access rights — police records, agency files, credit and health data — and the request that opens them.
themes.transfer_check: Submit (or fully prepare) one real access request to a public body for your own records, to its formal requirements.

themes.description: Benefits refused, permits denied, fines issued — reading the decision letter, the reasons, and the review and appeal ladder.
themes.transfer_check: Take one real or case-study adverse decision and draft the first-stage challenge inside its deadline, addressing the stated reasons.

themes.theme: Voting and the machinery of elections
themes.description: Registration, eligibility, the ballot's journey and the count — the process behind the cross in the box.
themes.transfer_check: Verify your own registration, explain your ballot's path from booth to count, and correctly handle one edge case (moving, absence, spoiled paper).

themes.theme: Jury service and the citizen's bench
themes.description: Selection, duties, deliberation and the juror's oath — the one week the justice system runs on you.
themes.transfer_check: From a case summary, deliberate in a mock jury to a verdict, applying the standard of proof and the judge's directions.

themes.description: Citizenship, residence and visas in outline — what status determines, and helping someone find competent immigration help.
themes.transfer_check: For one case-study person, identify what their status allows and bars, and locate the regulated adviser route for their question.

themes.description: Freedom of information, public meetings, complaints against officials and the press — the accountability toolkit in civilian hands.
themes.transfer_check: File (or fully draft) one real freedom-of-information request on a matter you care about, scoped so it cannot be refused as too broad.
